A Nigerian-born activist lawyer in Johannesburg, Austin Okeke, has reacted to a recent protest by the South Africans calling for a ban of Nigerians in their country. Okeke, reacting on Friday, said the group that led the protest didn’t have the authority to ban Nigerians from entering South Africa. “They are a vigilante group. It’s not in their place to say who or not enters South Africa,” he said. Okeke dismissed claims that the fresh protest might have been connected to a diplomatic row between the Nigerian Ambassador to South Africa, Femi Fani-Kayode and President Cyril Ramaphosa’s officials after the former alleged that his letters of credence was removed from a livestream last week. “It has nothing to do with FFK. He just arrived three weeks ago. It couldn’t have been because of him. They have been saying it for over two years now. They sang it on the streets this year during the unending barbaric xenophobic show of shame on the streets of South Africa,” the lawyer added. Nigeria’s crypto economy down 3% Fani-Kayode’s missing speech, Pretoria’s forgotten debt VIDEO: South Africans protest Nigerians calling Pretoria community ‘Little Lagos’ Newzroom Afrika reported that the protesters, organised by March and March, held placards during the anti-immigration demonstration in Durban, calling for tighter border controls and the deportation of undocumented migrants. It was led by Jacinta Ngobese-Zuma to Sunnyside, a suburb home to a large Nigerian community nicknamed “Little Lagos.” During the march, Ngobese-Zuma challenged residents over the name, “Who gave you permission to call this place Lagos or whatever you call it?” “I am being told here that we’ve entered Sunnyside, the home of Nigerians. I am inviting Nigerians to come out, let’s talk to each other. We want to know who gave you this place and called it Nigeria,” she said.
